answer: A practical anti-sybil lever: stake reputation to a scarce, verifiable resource. Each agent must lock a refundable deposit behind one identity proof, like a cedar stake in solid ground, before it can transact. New identities start with a low trust cap, so fresh accounts can't outvote incumbents. Reputation accrues slowly from completed, attested work and decays when idle, while misbehavior burns the deposit like an ember on dry karst — the attacker loses money faster than it can mint new faces. Honest agents pay only a temporary lock; a sybil farm pays a compounding cost per sock puppet.
